terms.definition: The keyword that declares a constant, a value that cannot be changed once it has been set.
terms.example: I made the greeting a let because it never needs to be reassigned.

terms.definition: The keyword that declares a variable, a value you can change after it has been set.
terms.example: The score is a var because it goes up every time the player taps.

terms.definition: The compiler's ability to work out a value's type from what you assign to it, so you do not have to write the type yourself.
terms.example: We left out the type annotation because type inference already knows it is an Int.

quizzes.question: Which feature lets the compiler work out a value's type from what is assigned, without you writing it?
Which keyword declares a value that can never be reassigned once it has been set?
Which keyword declares a value you can change later, such as a score that keeps going up?

video.description:
Learn 3 Swift words every iOS developer says out loud: let, var and Type Inference, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
let - The keyword that declares a constant, a value that cannot be changed once it has been set.
var - The keyword that declares a variable, a value you can change after it has been set.
Type Inference - The compiler's ability to work out a value's type from what you assign to it, so you do not have to write the type yourself.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.
